title: Change Pose by OBJ Morphing
content: **Objective** Vertex Morphing has a merit of maintaining avatar's final form without any distortion. However on the other hand, garments may fall off during the morphing process, especially when there is a large difference between the first and the last pose as the pose changes by the minimum distances between points in the avatar rather than the units of avatar joints. Therefore if a big difference between the poses, it is recommended to create an OBJ file for interim pose and morph stage-by-stage. If it is inconvenience, change pose by another method, [Change Pose by Using Collada](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002633147). **Operation** 1. After dressing an avatar in CLO, at least two files are required to change poses such as T-pose avatar and another avatar in desired pose. Export both of the files in OBJ format. To find export method in details, check [3D File (OBJ) Import/Export ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107) for the reference. 2. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ** and select the T-pose OBJ file of the previously exported avatar. Click **OK** on the option dialogue to load the avatar. 3. Put the garments on top of the loaded avatar. 4. Click File ▶ Import ▶ **Morph Target** and load the previously saved avatar with another pose. Set the 'Morphing Frame Count' in the option dialogue, then click **OK**. 5. The **Simulation** button automatically activates and the avatar pose slowly changes according to the set frame count. The garment also starts simulating in accordance with the change. Adjust garments if necessary, after the final pose simulation.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using Vertex Morphing to change avatar poses in CLO while ensuring garments remain intact throughout the process.

title: [3D Tool] Free Sewing
content: ### **Objective** In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Free Sewing ** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001254128/_______.png) **Free Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing ** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001254128/_______.png) **Free Sewing ** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click, drag and double click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. 3. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. → Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. 4. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. 5. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. **※ Note:** * The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. * Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. * Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference [M:N Free Sewing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001754668).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Free Sewing feature in 3D design software to establish Sewing Lines on pattern outlines and internal shapes.

title: [3D Tool] 1:N Free Sewing
content: **Objective ** In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns to a single Pattern. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244107/_______.png) **Free Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001244107/_______.png) **Free Sewing** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish the start and the end point on the Pattern outline, which is called as 1, where multiple Patterns are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Line appears in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key, establish Sewing Lines on N Patterns. Similar to setting regular Free Sewing Lines, be careful with Directional Notches. 5. Release the Shift key to complete. **※ Note** * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions.
content_description: The purpose of this webpage is to guide users through the process of establishing Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes in both 2D and 3D environments for seamless pattern integration.

title: [3D Tool] 1:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (N) to a single segment (1.) If the total length of N segments and the length of 1 segment are different, the 1 segment is equally divided by the number of N segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290728/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290728/_______.png) **Segment Sewing** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Select a single segment which multiple segments are sewn to. 3. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While holding down the Shift key on the keyboard, drag the mouse to hover over the N segments. Before clicking the segment, be careful to make Directional Notches parallel to each other. 5. Then, click on the segments to establish Sewing Lines on the N segments. 6. Release the Shift key to complete the 1:N Segment Sewing. **※ Note** * While establishing N Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for users to efficiently sew multiple segments to a single segment in a 3D environment, ensuring precise alignment and structure.

title: [3D Tool] M:N Free Sewing
content: **Objective** In the 3D window, freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines to sew multiple Patterns (M) to multiple Patterns (N) at once. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005448927/M_N________.png) **M:N Free Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Free Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Free Sewing** Tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Free Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005448927/M_N________.png) **M:N Free Sewing** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Establish Free Sewing Lines on multiple Patterns, which are considered as M Patterns. 3. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines appear in neon color. 4. While being mindful of Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on Patterns which are sewn to M Patterns. Hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M:N Sewing Lines. → All Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing the Sewing Lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * While establishing M:N sewing lines, if you click on an inappropriate segment, the segment appears in red and the Sewing Line cannot be applied. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover how to efficiently create and manage Sewing Lines between multiple Patterns in both 2D and 3D environments using the M:N Free Sewing tool.

title: [3D Tool] M:N Segment Sewing
content: **Objective** In the 3D window, easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing** **※ Note:** Hold down the **Segment Sewing** tool for a while to access the **M:N Segment Sewing** tool. ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ **M:N Segment Sewing** 2D or 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001290748/M_N________.png) **M:N Segment Sewing ** → All sew-able segments are bolded. → All Sewing Lines appear in both 2D and 3D windows. 2. Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. → M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. 3. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. → The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. **※ Note:** * While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. * When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The M:N Segment Sewing tool allows users to efficiently sew and edit multiple segments in a 3D environment, automatically adjusting segment lengths to ensure accurate alignment.

title: [Popup] Copy/Paste Tack
content: **List of Contents** Copy/Paste Tack Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern ### **Objective** Copy and paste tack. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001105367/_______.png) **Edit Tack** ** Operation** **Copy/Paste Tack** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001105367/_______.png) **Edit Tack** → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be copied and pasted. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Copy** → The selected tack is copied. 4. Access the right-click pop-up menu again on the copied tack. 5. Select**Paste** or **Mirror Paste**. → Preview of the selected tack follows the mouse cursor in 2D and 3D windows. → Any tack outside of the Pattern do not appear in the 3D window. 6. Click the desired location to paste the tack. ** Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ **Edit Tack** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001105367/_______.png) **Edit Tack** → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select **Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern**. → Selected tack is duplicated to the exact same location on its Symmetric Pattern. ※Note: Select tacks need to be within the same Pattern in order to be duplicated to their Symmetric Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to copy, paste, and duplicate tacks within the sewing design software for creating symmetric patterns.

title: [Tool] Create Buttonholes along Pattern Outline (ver5.1.0)
content: **List of Contents** Create Select Unlink ### **Objective** Create buttonholess along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Buttonhole** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Buttonhole** ** Operation** **Create** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Buttonhole** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Buttonhole** 2. Right click on a Pattern Outline. → The **Create Buttons/Buttonholes along Pattern Outline** window appears. **※Note:** To select multiple lines, press down the Shift key and click the lines to be selected. 3. Configure below options as needed: **Start Position** | Distance | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the selected line. ---|---|--- Interval | Set the distance between the buttonholes and the Pattern Outline. Reverse | The direction of which buttonholes are created is reversed to the Start Point. ** Replicate ** | Interval | Adjust the distance between the buttonholes. Number of Button/Buttonholes | Adjust the number of buttonholes to be created. 4. Click **OK**. → Buttonholes are created as a group. **Select** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Buttonhole** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Buttonhole** 2. Click on a buttonhole or a Pattern Outline where buttonholes are created. → All buttonholes in a group are selected. **※Note:** Click again while the group of buttonholes are selected to select a single buttonhole. 3. Change selected buttonholes' [properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002382548) or [style](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000717067-Buttonhole-Style-Properties) or use [right-click pop-up menu](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001042867). → Any changes made are applied to all buttonholes in the same group. → Group information cannot be copied or duplicated. **※Note:** Grouped buttonholes cannot be moved. **Unlink** 1. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Select/Move Button** 2. Right click on the buttonholes or the Pattern Outline and select **Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes**. → The link between the buttonholes are removed. ** ** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating, selecting, and unlinking buttonholes along a pattern outline in a 3D design environment.

title: [Popup] Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern
content: ### **Objective** Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015218607/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png) **Select/Move Button** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Select/Move Button** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115015218607/Toolbar_3D_Button_Edit.png) **Select/Move Button** 2. Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. → The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. 3. Right click on the selected button or buttonhole. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 4. Depending on the selected item, select **Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern** or **Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern**. → The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for duplicating buttons and buttonholes in a symmetrical pattern using the 3D Toolbar in the CLO 3D software.

title: [Style Property] Edit Puckering Style Properties
content: **List of Contents** Puckering Style Setting Default Puckering Style **Objective** Edit or reset Puckering style properties. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab ** Operation ** **Puckering Style Setting** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab 2. Click on Puckering style. → Puckering style properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Adjust the properties as needed. **Name** | Name the Puckering style. ---|--- **Material** | Five presets are provided: Cotton, Denim, Leather, Nylon, Polyester. **Texture (ver.5.1.0)** | Apply the texture. **Desaturation** | Maintain the texture of images or patterns while changing colors. **Shadow Intensity** | Adjust the intensity of the texture's shadow. **Shadow Brightness** | Adjust the brightness of the texture's shadow while maintaining the image's pattern and texture. **Normal Map** | Change the Puckering's shape by importing a Normal Map. **Opacity (%)** | Adjust the Normal Map's opacity. **Specification** | **Density (%)** | Adjust the density of the Normal Map. **Width (mm)** | Adjust the width of the Normal Map. **Default Puckering Style** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab 2. Right click on the puckering style to make as a default, and click **Reset**. → The selected puckering style's properties are reset to the Default Puckering's. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides instructions for editing and resetting puckering style properties within the Object Browser's Puckering Tab.

title: [Property] Scale Avatars (ver 5.2)
content: **Objective** Scale an OBJ imported as an Avatar. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f78wmVjhuCc **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment**▶ Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024215067/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move ** ** Operation** 1. [Import an OBJ as an Avatar.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107) 2. Select the tool/ menu indicated in Location. 3. title: Connection to DMIx Cloud & Compatible with Material (ver 6.0)
content: **Objective** Simply drag and drop to apply color or AxF files for CLO. Find a variety of digitalized materials & colors from DMIx Cloud Web of Color Digital. **** **Operation** 1. Drag and drop AxF files into the 3D/ 2D window of CLO from the DMIx Cloud webpage. → The AxF files are downloaded in DMIx Download Manager. 2. Drag and drop AxF files to the 3D garment/ 2D Patterns or Click '**Assign to Selected Fabric** ' in **DMIx Download Manager** once you selected 3D garment/2D patterns. → AxF file is applied. **※ Note: ** * Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Clicking **DMIx Download Manager** also allows you to execute the window. * New items are added when you drag and drop the AxF file of **DMIx Download Manager** to the **Fabric** **List**.
content_description: Easily enhance your CLO designs by dragging and dropping color or AxF files from the DMIx Cloud Web of Color Digital.

title: Iridescence Material Expression (ver 6.0)
content: **Objective** Different colors of light are reflected depending on the angle of the screen. Holographic foil, vinyl, pearls, shells of shellfish can be expressed. The application result can be checked only in the render window. **Location** Fabric Property Editor▶ Material ▶ Type ▶ Iridescence**(Render Only)** ** Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location.** ****** 2. Edit the properties by referring to the table below. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- Color (1-5) | Set the color of each area to be reflected according to the 3D screen angle. Roughness | Adjust the roughness of the object surface. Hue Shift | Shift the entire color spectrum to a different hue changing the 5 colors together. Weight | Adjust the weight to reflect the set color on the object surface. 3. [Run](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747-Run-V-Ray-Render) the render window. → The iridescent material is applied
content_description: This web page serves as a guide for using the Fabric Property Editor to create and customize iridescent materials in a 3D rendering environment.

title: User Setting (CFG) Open/Save
content: **List of Contents** Save Open **Objective** Save user settings such as language, measurement units, and shortcuts as a configuration file that can be applied to program updates. ** Location ** **Save** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **User Setting** **Open ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **User Setting** **Operation ** **Save** 1. Configure the [user settings](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000732727) as needed. 2. Locate the menu as below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **User Setting** → The Save File window appears. 3. Assign the file name and location, then click **Save**. → The user settings is saved as a configuration file. **Open ** 1. Locate the menu as below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **User Setting** → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired configuration file and hit the **Open** button. → The information window appears, asking you to restart the program to apply the changes. 3. Restart the program. → The user settings contained within the configuration file is applied. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving and opening user settings as configuration files, allowing users to easily manage their preferences for program updates.

title: Trim (TRM) Open/Save
content: **List of Contents** Save Open **Objective** Save OBJ files as Trim files. Trim files can be previewed in the CLO Library and can [be glued to the Garment.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000526728-%EB%B6%80%EC%9E%90%EC%9E%AC-%EB%B6%99%EC%9D%B4%EA%B8%B0). ** Location ** **Save** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶**Trim** **Open ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Trim** **Operation ** **Save** 1. [Load an OBJ file as Trim](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000494107-3D-%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-OBJ-%EB%B6%88%EB%9F%AC%EC%98%A4%EA%B8%B0-%EB%82%B4%EB%B3%B4%EB%82%B4%EA%B8%B0#Click4). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶**Trim** → When there are multiple OBJs in the 3D window, tje Save Trim window appears allowing you to choose the desired OBJ. → The Save File window appears. 3. Locate the saving path and file name. Then, click the **Save** button. → The OBJ file is saved Trim file. **Open** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below : Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Trim** → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the file to be opened and click **Open**. → The Open Trim window appears. 3. Use the drop-down menu next to **Position** option to locate the Trim. → **Original:** trim is loaded at its original position when it was saved as a Trim file. → **Reset:** trim is loaded at the center of the 3D window. ※ Note: * Hover the mouse over the Trim file in the Library window to preview trim. * Click and drag or double lick the Trim file to open from the Library window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to save and open OBJ files as Trim files for use in the CLO Library, enabling easy previewing and application to garments.

title: Animation Video Capture
content: ### **Objective** Create video captures of animations recorded in the Animation Mode. ### **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Animation** ### **Operation** 1. Navigate to the Animation Mode. → The screen environment changes to Animation Mode. 2. [Record an animation](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000559488). 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Animation** → The Animation window with video capture settings appears. 4. Adjust the settings below as needed: Menu Item | Description ---|--- Video Size | Preset | Select from available presets for the video capture size. Orientation | Select the video capture orientation. Width | Input a specific pixel width for the video capture. Height | Input a specific pixel height for the video capture. Video Codec | Set the codec to use when recording video. **※ Note: **From ver 6.0, it is available to save MP4/AVI for Windows and MOV files for MAC without installing a separate codec. 5. Click on the **Record** button. → The animation video capture automatically starts from the beginning of the recorded Garment animation. 6. Click on the **Stop** button. → The animation video capture is completed and a preview window appears. 7. Click on the **Save** button in the preview window. → Navigate to a desired file location and input a desired file name in the window that appears. 8. Click on the **Save** button after navigating to the desired file location. → The animation video capture is saved. **※ Note:** While video recording, the main menu, 3D view controls, and Animation Editor functions cannot be used. Press the **Pause** button to pause the recording, then use the view controls to change the view, or use other functions. However, it is impossible to switch to other modes. To stop the video capture altogether, press Esc on the keyboard, click on **Cancel** , or **X** button on the top-right corner.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for capturing video recordings of animations in Animation Mode, including settings adjustments and saving options.

title: Motion (MTN) Open/Save
content: **Objective** Motion is a native file format (*mtn) of CLO that saves Avatar movement information, and is used when recording Animation of Garments and Avatars. CLO provides Motion files for its default male and female Avatars, but Animation Data or Motion capture Data from third-party 3D solutions can be imported as COLLADA files, then extracted as a Motion file (*mtn) through this menu. ** Location** **Open Motion** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Joint Motion** **Save Motion** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Joint Motion** ** Operation** **Open Motion** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Joint Motion** → The Open File window appears. 2. Navigate to the desired *mtn file, then click **Open**. → The Load Motion Type window appears. 3. Select from the available settings: **Garment Position** | **Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position** | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver 2.5.0). ---|---|--- **Transition Animation** | A transition Animation is an Animation that changes from a T-Pose to a motion's first Pose in stages, and is created when the Avatar's current Pose and Motion differs from that of the first frame Pose. → The motion (*mtn) file loads according to the settings. **Save Motion** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Joint Motion** → The Save File window appears. 2. Type in file name and designate the path the file will be saved to. → The Motion (*mtn) file will be saved to the designated path. **※ Note:** * Motion files can only be saved when imported as Avatars in COLLADA format with Motion Data, and the COLLADA files must be in Open COLLADA format. * To learn more about COLLADA format, please reference [3D File (COLLADA) Import](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000531948-3D%ED%8C%8C%EC%9D%BC-COLLADA-%EB%B6%88%EB%9F%AC%EC%98%A4%EA%B8%B0).
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to open and save Motion files (*mtn) in CLO, detailing the steps for managing Avatar movements and importing animation data from COLLADA files.

title: USB Plotter (ver 6.0)
content: **List of Contents** Plotter Share Settings Add Plotter Network ### **Objective** Install a Plotter of USB type to print the pattern. Install the driver for the connected plotter. Install the correct driver for the connected plotter model from each manufacturer's website. ** ** **** ### **Operation ** **Plotter Share Settings ** 1. Select the **Settings** by clicking the Start on the taskbar. 2. Select **Devices** and click the **Printers & Scanners** on the left → A list of connected printers and scanners appears. 3. After selecting the installed plotter, manage ▶ Printer Properties ▶ Sharing Tab ▶ Share this printer 4. After completing the settings, [print the pattern to the plotter.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001557927-Plot-Patterns-Above-ver4-2-0-) **Add Plotter Network** Add a share plotter from another computer connected to the same internet network. 1. Open File Explorer, enter **Network** in the address bar. 2. Click the computer where the plotter is connected to. → The plotter appears in the list of File Explorer. 3. Click the Plotter → The driver installation window appears. 4. Click **install the driver.** → The driver is installed and the plotter is added to the list of printers and scanners. 5. After completing the setting, [print the pattern to the plotter.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001557927-Plot-Patterns-Above-ver4-2-0-)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for installing and configuring a USB plotter for seamless pattern printing and network sharing.

title: Comment Mode
content: **Comment Mode YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mdRKuFpZdpw** **-** Write in comments in the Comment Mode. \- Comment Mode ▶ Main Menu ▶ **Comment.** \- Click on the 3D Garment where a comment should be added. \- An active comment window appears and you may type in contents. \- Click OK to complete the comment. **※Note:** Comment mode will not be supported in the next version of CLO to develop more various functions. Please use the 'Annotation' function of the newly developed CLO-SET.
content_description: "Explore how to use Comment Mode to enhance your experience with CLO's 3D Garment features, while transitioning to the new Annotation function in CLO-SET for future updates."
